title: 01. Quick start
text: full workflow one block.
code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Load the data data("landscape_counts"); data("surv_pts") pts       <- vect(surv_pts) land_rast <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                               package = "multiScaleR"))  # 2. Prepare the kernel inputs kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast,                              max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian")  # 3. Fit a starting model df  <- data.frame(landscape_counts, kernel_inputs$kernel_dat) mod <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, family = poisson(), data = df)  # 4. Estimate the scales of effect opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod, kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs)  # 5. Read the results summary(opt)                   # sigma, effective distance, regression table summary(opt, profile = TRUE)   # profile-likelihood intervals for sigma (slower) kernel_dist(opt)               # radius holding 90% of the kernel weight exp(coef(opt$opt_mod))         # multiplicative change in expected count plot(opt)                      # kernel weight against distance plot(opt, add_label = FALSE)   # the same plot without the text beneath it plot_marginal_effects(opt)     # expected count across each covariate plot(profile_sigma(opt))       # AICc across sigma: is each scale identified?  # 6. Map the fitted model r_scaled <- kernel_scale.raster(land_rast, multiScaleR = opt,                                 scale_center = TRUE, clamp = TRUE) pred <- terra::predict(r_scaled, opt$opt_mod, type = "response")

code: set.seed(12345) zi_rast <- sim_rast(user_seed = 999, dim = 500, resolution = 30) zi_rast <- subset(zi_rast, c("bin1", "cont1"))   # one binary, one continuous layer  # 400 random points at least 1,000 m inside the raster edge interior <- buffer(vect(ext(zi_rast)), -1000) zi_pts   <- spatSample(zi_rast[[1]], size = 400, method = "random",                        ext = ext(interior), as.points = TRUE)  # Covariates weighted at the true scales: 400 m for bin1, 200 m for cont1 truth <- kernel_prep(pts = zi_pts, raster_stack = zi_rast, max_D = 1500,                      kernel = "gaussian", sigma = c(400, 200),                      verbose = FALSE)$kernel_dat  # Excess zeros depend on cont1. Counts depend on bin1 excess_zero <- rbinom(400, size = 1, prob = plogis(-0.25 - 1 * truth$cont1)) abundance   <- rnbinom(400, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.75 * truth$bin1), size = 2) zi_dat      <- data.frame(cnt = ifelse(excess_zero == 1, 0, abundance))  # Prepare the inputs without telling the package the true scales zi_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = zi_pts, raster_stack = zi_rast, max_D = 1500,                          kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE) zi_df <- data.frame(zi_dat, zi_inputs$kernel_dat)  # Count model | zero-inflation model zinb_mod <- pscl::zeroinfl(cnt ~ bin1 | cont1, dist = "negbin", data = zi_df) zinb_opt <- multiScale_optim(zinb_mod, zi_inputs, verbose = FALSE) round(summary(zinb_opt)$opt_scale)      # sigma (m): truth is 400 and 200 #>       Mean SE 2.5% 97.5% #> bin1   289 48  194   383 #> cont1  141 51   41   240 round(coef(zinb_opt$opt_mod), 2)        # truth: 0.5, 0.75, -0.25, -1 #> count_(Intercept)        count_bin1  zero_(Intercept)        zero_cont1  #>              0.64              0.80              0.12             -0.92

code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Understand the kernel plot_kernel(sigma = 300, kernel = "gaussian", add_label = FALSE) kernel_dist(sigma = 300, kernel = "gaussian")      # radius with 90% of the weight  # 2. Prepare the data data("landscape_counts"); data("surv_pts") dat       <- landscape_counts pts       <- vect(surv_pts) land_rast <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                               package = "multiScaleR")) kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast,                              max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian")  # 3. Fit a starting model and estimate the scales df  <- data.frame(dat, kernel_inputs$kernel_dat) mod <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, family = poisson(), data = df) opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod, kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs)  # 4. Read and check the fit summary(opt)                                # sigma, distance, coefficients, warnings summary(opt, profile = TRUE)                # profile-likelihood limits for sigma kernel_dist(opt)                            # effective distance (map units) plot(opt)                                   # fitted kernels plot(opt, prob = 0.99, add_label = FALSE)   # 99% radius, no text under panels plot_marginal_effects(opt)                  # expected response across covariates plot(profile_sigma(opt, n_pts = 15))        # is each scale identified?  # 5. Guard against a stalled search (a fixed kernel screens starts by default) fixed_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast,                             max_D = 1700, kernel = "fixed") set.seed(1) opt_fixed <- multiScale_optim(mod, fixed_inputs)  # 6. Compare models (each sigma counts as a parameter) mod_land <- glm(counts ~ land1 + land2, family = poisson(), data = df) opt_land <- multiScale_optim(mod_land, kernel_inputs) aic_tab(list(opt, opt_land), mod_names = c("site + land1 + land2",                                            "land1 + land2"))  # 7. Other families: same workflow, different starting model mod_nb     <- MASS::glm.nb(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, data = df) df$present <- as.integer(df$counts > 0) mod_bin    <- glm(present ~ site + land1 + land2,                   family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = df) opt_nb     <- multiScale_optim(mod_nb,  kernel_inputs) opt_bin    <- multiScale_optim(mod_bin, kernel_inputs) # pscl::zeroinfl(cnt ~ bin1 | cont1, dist = "negbin", data = zi_df) # unmarked::pcount(~ 1 ~ bin1 + cont2, data = nmix_umf, K = 100) # unmarked::occu(~ 1 ~ bin1 + cont2, data = occ_umf)  # 8. Map the fitted model r_scaled <- kernel_scale.raster(raster_stack = land_rast, multiScaleR = opt,                                 scale_center = TRUE, clamp = TRUE) pred <- terra::predict(r_scaled, opt$opt_mod, type = "response")

code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Fit the model data("landscape_counts"); data("surv_pts") pts       <- vect(surv_pts) land_rast <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                               package = "multiScaleR")) inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast, max_D = 1700,                       kernel = "gaussian", bin = TRUE) df     <- data.frame(landscape_counts, inputs$kernel_dat) start  <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, family = poisson(), data = df) fit    <- multiScale_optim(start, inputs, backend = "profile_glm", n_cores = 1)  # 2. Project without clamping and predict r_unclamped <- kernel_scale.raster(land_rast, multiScaleR = fit,                                    scale_center = TRUE, clamp = FALSE) pred_unclamped <- terra::predict(r_unclamped, fit$opt_mod, type = "response")  # 3. Map the cells outside the surveyed range covs <- c("land1", "land2") lim  <- sapply(fit$opt_mod$model[covs], range)     # survey min and max out_land1 <- r_unclamped$land1 < lim[1, "land1"] |              r_unclamped$land1 > lim[2, "land1"] out_land2 <- r_unclamped$land2 < lim[1, "land2"] |              r_unclamped$land2 > lim[2, "land2"] outside   <- out_land1 | out_land2 plot(outside)                                      # where the model extrapolates 100 * global(outside, "mean")[1, 1]                # percent of the map  # 4. Clamp to the surveyed range and predict again r_clamped <- kernel_scale.raster(land_rast, multiScaleR = fit,                                  scale_center = TRUE, clamp = TRUE) pred_clamped <- terra::predict(r_clamped, fit$opt_mod, type = "response") plot(pred_clamped / pred_unclamped)                # 1 = unchanged by clamping  # 5. Narrow or widen the limits r_narrow <- kernel_scale.raster(land_rast, multiScaleR = fit,                                 scale_center = TRUE, clamp = TRUE,                                 pct_mx = -0.1)     # limits move inward r_wide   <- kernel_scale.raster(land_rast, multiScaleR = fit,                                 scale_center = TRUE, clamp = TRUE,                                 pct_mx = 0.1)      # limits move outward

title: 04. Landscape Metrics as Covariates
code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Load the data and build a categorical layer data("landscape_counts"); data("surv_pts") dat       <- landscape_counts pts       <- vect(surv_pts) land_rast <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                               package = "multiScaleR")) landcover <- classify(land_rast$land3,                       rcl = matrix(c(-Inf, 0.45, 1,                                      0.45, 0.55, 2,                                      0.55,  Inf, 3), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)) names(landcover) <- "landcover" metric_rasters <- c(land_rast$land1, land_rast$land2, landcover)  # 2. Define the covariates: two kernel means and two fixed-radius metrics scale_vars <- msr_vars(   land1_prop     = kernel_var("land1"),   land2_mean     = kernel_var("land2"),   land1_ed_500   = landscape_var("land1", metric = "ed", radius = 500),   cover_shdi_500 = landscape_var("landcover", metric = "shdi", radius = 500) )  # 3. Compute the covariates at the survey points kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = metric_rasters,                              max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian",                              scale_vars = scale_vars, verbose = FALSE) kernel_inputs$scl_params            # mean and SD of each metric, in its units  # 4. Fit the model and estimate the kernel scales df  <- data.frame(dat, kernel_inputs$kernel_dat) mod <- glm(counts ~ site + land1_prop + land2_mean +              land1_ed_500 + cover_shdi_500,            family = poisson(), data = df) opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod, kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs,                         verbose = FALSE) summary(opt)                        # sigma, effective distance, regression table  # 5. Read a metric coefficient in the metric's units beta <- coef(opt$opt_mod) sds  <- opt$scl_params$sd exp(beta["land1_ed_500"] * 10 / sds["land1_ed_500"])   # per 10 m/ha of edge  # 6. Estimate the radius of a metric: leave radius out set.seed(1) truth_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast["land1"],                             max_D = 1200, verbose = FALSE,                             scale_vars = msr_vars(                               ed_400 = landscape_var("land1", metric = "ed",                                                      radius = 400))) sim_counts  <- rpois(100, exp(0.5 + 0.5 * truth_inputs$kernel_dat$ed_400)) free_vars   <- msr_vars(land1_ed = landscape_var("land1", metric = "ed")) free_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast["land1"],                            max_D = 1200, scale_vars = free_vars,                            verbose = FALSE) sim_df  <- data.frame(counts = sim_counts, free_inputs$kernel_dat) sim_mod <- glm(counts ~ land1_ed, family = poisson(), data = sim_df) sim_opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = sim_mod, kernel_inputs = free_inputs,                             verbose = FALSE) summary(sim_opt, profile = TRUE)$opt_scale     # radius with profile limits plot(profile_sigma(sim_opt, n_pts = 15, verbose = FALSE))   # AICc by radius grid_fit <- multiScale_optim(sim_mod, free_inputs, backend = "refit",                              radius_grid = seq(200, 1000, by = 100)) diagnostics(grid_fit)$radius_profile        # log-likelihood at each listed radius plot_marginal_effects(sim_opt)                 # expected count against m/ha  # 7. Map the covariates of a fitted model, or a metric on its own projected <- kernel_scale.raster(raster_stack = metric_rasters,                                  multiScaleR = opt, verbose = FALSE) ed_multi  <- kernel_scale.raster(   raster_stack = metric_rasters["land1"],   scale_vars   = msr_vars(     ed_200 = landscape_var("land1", metric = "ed", radius = 200),     ed_500 = landscape_var("land1", metric = "ed", radius = 500),     ed_900 = landscape_var("land1", metric = "ed", radius = 900)),   verbose = FALSE)

title: 05. Surface Texture Metrics as Covariates
code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Load the data data("landscape_counts"); data("surv_pts") dat       <- landscape_counts pts       <- vect(surv_pts) land_rast <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                               package = "multiScaleR"))  # 2. Define the covariates: two kernel means and one fixed-radius metric scale_vars <- msr_vars(   land1_prop   = kernel_var("land1"),   land2_mean   = kernel_var("land2"),   land3_sq_500 = surface_var("land3", metric = "sq", radius = 500) )  # 3. Compute the covariates at the survey points kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast,                              max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian",                              scale_vars = scale_vars, verbose = FALSE) kernel_inputs$scl_params            # mean and SD of each metric, in its units  # 4. Fit the model and estimate the kernel scales df  <- data.frame(dat, kernel_inputs$kernel_dat) mod <- glm(counts ~ site + land1_prop + land2_mean + land3_sq_500,            family = poisson(), data = df) opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod, kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs,                         verbose = FALSE) summary(opt)                        # sigma, effective distance, regression table  # 5. Read a metric coefficient in the metric's units beta <- coef(opt$opt_mod) sds  <- opt$scl_params$sd exp(beta["land3_sq_500"] * 0.01 / sds["land3_sq_500"])   # per 0.01 of roughness  # 6. Estimate the scale of a metric: weight it with the kernel weighted_vars <- msr_vars(   land3_sq = surface_var("land3", metric = "sq", weighted = TRUE) ) truth_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast["land3"],                             max_D = 1500, kernel = "gaussian",                             scale_vars = weighted_vars, sigma = 300,                             verbose = FALSE) set.seed(1) sim_counts  <- rpois(100, exp(0.5 + 0.5 * truth_inputs$kernel_dat$land3_sq)) free_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast["land3"],                            max_D = 1500, kernel = "gaussian",                            scale_vars = weighted_vars, verbose = FALSE) sim_df  <- data.frame(counts = sim_counts, free_inputs$kernel_dat) sim_mod <- glm(counts ~ land3_sq, family = poisson(), data = sim_df) sim_opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = sim_mod, kernel_inputs = free_inputs,                             verbose = FALSE) summary(sim_opt)$opt_scale                     # sigma, SE, and 95% interval kernel_dist(sim_opt)                           # radius holding 90% of the weight plot(profile_sigma(sim_opt, n_pts = 15, verbose = FALSE))   # AICc by sigma plot_marginal_effects(sim_opt)                 # expected count against roughness  # 7. Map the covariates of a fitted model, or a metric on its own projected <- kernel_scale.raster(raster_stack = land_rast,                                  multiScaleR = opt, verbose = FALSE) sq_multi  <- kernel_scale.raster(   raster_stack = land_rast["land3"],   scale_vars   = msr_vars(     sq_200 = surface_var("land3", metric = "sq", radius = 200),     sq_500 = surface_var("land3", metric = "sq", radius = 500),     sq_900 = surface_var("land3", metric = "sq", radius = 900)),   verbose = FALSE) sq_weighted <- kernel_scale.raster(   raster_stack = land_rast["land3"],   scale_vars   = msr_vars(sq_weighted = surface_var("land3", metric = "sq",                                                     weighted = TRUE)),   sigma = 500, kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)

code: data("surv_pts") pts  <- vect(surv_pts)     # 100 survey locations as a terra SpatVector land <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                          package = "multiScaleR"))  # The bundled objects carry no coordinate reference system (CRS). # Assign the same projected CRS, in meters, to both. crs(pts)  <- "EPSG:26915" crs(land) <- "EPSG:26915"  # Year 1: the binary habitat layer (1 = habitat, 0 = not habitat) habitat_1 <- land$land1 names(habitat_1) <- "habitat"  # Year 2: the same map after habitat is cleared from one square habitat_2 <- habitat_1 cleared   <- ext(1000, 2600, 1400, 3000) habitat_2[cells(habitat_2, cleared)] <- 0  # One row per observation, with the year of its survey: 50 points per year set.seed(93) obs <- data.frame(year = factor(sample(rep(c("year1", "year2"), each = 50)))) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(habitat_1, main = "Year 1", legend = FALSE) points(pts[obs$year == "year1", ], pch = 19, cex = 0.5, col = "red") plot(habitat_2, main = "Year 2", legend = FALSE) points(pts[obs$year == "year2", ], pch = 19, cex = 0.5, col = "red") lines(vect(cleared), col = "red", lwd = 2)   # outline of the cleared square par(op) # Kernel-weighted habitat at the true scale (sigma = 250 m) on each map true_1 <- kernel_scale.raster(habitat_1, sigma = 250, kernel = "gaussian",                               verbose = FALSE) true_2 <- kernel_scale.raster(habitat_2, sigma = 250, kernel = "gaussian",                               verbose = FALSE)  # Read each point's value from the map of its own year hab <- ifelse(obs$year == "year1",               extract(true_1, pts)[, 2],               extract(true_2, pts)[, 2]) hab_z <- (hab - mean(hab)) / sd(hab)    # standardize across all 100 rows  # Poisson counts: habitat lowers the expected count, year 2 raises it obs$count <- rpois(nrow(obs),                    exp(0.25 - 0.5 * hab_z + 0.3 * (obs$year == "year2")))

title: 06. Using Year-Specific Rasters in One Model
code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Align the annual maps: one grid, one projected CRS, matching layer names data("surv_pts") pts  <- vect(surv_pts) land <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                          package = "multiScaleR")) crs(pts)  <- "EPSG:26915" crs(land) <- "EPSG:26915" habitat_1 <- land$land1 names(habitat_1) <- "habitat" habitat_2 <- habitat_1 cleared   <- ext(1000, 2600, 1400, 3000) habitat_2[cells(habitat_2, cleared)] <- 0  # 2. Label each observation with its year (and add your response, here `count`) set.seed(93) obs <- data.frame(year = factor(sample(rep(c("year1", "year2"), each = 50))))  # 3. Assign each observation to its map and prepare pooled covariates prepared <- kernel_prep_by_group(   pts = pts, raster_stacks = list(year1 = habitat_1, year2 = habitat_2),   group = obs$year, max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian",   store_cell_data = FALSE )  # 4. Fit one scale of effect and one habitat coefficient across years model_data <- data.frame(obs, prepared$kernel_dat) start <- glm(count ~ habitat + year, family = poisson(), data = model_data) fit   <- multiScale_optim(start, prepared, n_cores = 1) summary(fit)                           # shared sigma, distance, coefficients kernel_dist(fit)                       # radius holding 90% of the kernel weight diagnostics(fit)$sample_size           # rows prepared and rows fitted  # 5. Map the fitted model onto each year surface_1 <- kernel_scale.raster(habitat_1, multiScaleR = fit,                                  scale_center = TRUE,                                  site_values  = list(year = "year1")) surface_2 <- kernel_scale.raster(habitat_2, multiScaleR = fit,                                  scale_center = TRUE,                                  site_values  = list(year = "year2")) pred_1 <- terra::predict(surface_1, fit$opt_mod, type = "response") pred_2 <- terra::predict(surface_2, fit$opt_mod, type = "response") plot(pred_2 / pred_1)                  # change in expected count between years

code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Prepare once. Binned inputs serve every route. data("landscape_counts"); data("surv_pts") pts       <- vect(surv_pts) land_rast <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                               package = "multiScaleR")) inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast, max_D = 1700,                       kernel = "gaussian", bin = TRUE) df     <- data.frame(landscape_counts, inputs$kernel_dat) start  <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, family = poisson(), data = df)  # 2. Same model, two routes fit_refit   <- multiScale_optim(start, inputs)               # any model class fit_profile <- multiScale_optim(start, inputs, backend = "profile_glm",                                 n_cores = 1)                 # joint intervals summary(fit_refit)$opt_scale       # sigma, SE, symmetric 95% interval (m) summary(fit_profile)$opt_scale     # sigma, SE, 95% interval on the log scale  # 3. Prediction uncertainty by route predict(fit_refit, se.fit = TRUE, uncertainty = "conditional")       # scales fixed predict(fit_profile, interval = "confidence", uncertainty = "joint") # scales uncertain  # 4. Splines: written-out knots for profile_glm, either recipe for refit start_knots <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 +                      splines::ns(land2, knots = c(-0.5, 0.5),                                  Boundary.knots = c(-4, 4)),                    family = poisson(), data = df) start_df    <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + splines::ns(land2, df = 3),                    family = poisson(), data = df) fit_knots <- multiScale_optim(start_knots, inputs, backend = "profile_glm",                               n_cores = 1) fit_df    <- multiScale_optim(start_df, inputs) aic_tab(list(fit_profile, fit_knots, fit_df),         mod_names = c("linear", "spline, fixed knots", "spline, df = 3"))  # 5. Mixed covariate types: two estimated scales and one fixed-radius metric features <- msr_vars(   land1  = kernel_var("land1"),   land2  = kernel_var("land2"),   rough3 = surface_var("land3", "sa", radius = 300) ) inputs_mix <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land_rast, max_D = 1700,                           kernel = "gaussian", scale_vars = features,                           bin = TRUE) df_mix    <- data.frame(landscape_counts, inputs_mix$kernel_dat) start_mix <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + land2 + rough3,                  family = poisson(), data = df_mix) fit_mix_refit   <- multiScale_optim(start_mix, inputs_mix) fit_mix_profile <- multiScale_optim(start_mix, inputs_mix,                                     backend = "profile_glm", n_cores = 1)  # 6. Check a Bayesian model without fitting it bayes_check <- multiScale_bayes(counts ~ site + land1 + land2,                                 inputs = inputs, data = landscape_counts,                                 family = "poisson", method = "prepare")

code: set.seed(10) site        <- factor(rep(sprintf("site%02d", 1:18), each = 8))   # 18 sites habitat     <- rnorm(length(site))                       # standardized habitat site_effect <- rnorm(nlevels(site), sd = 0.7)[site]      # one value per site surveys <- data.frame(site, habitat, visit = rep(1:8, nlevels(site))) surveys$count <- rpois(nrow(surveys), exp(0.9 + 0.4 * habitat + site_effect))  # New sites: all eight visits to a site are held out together new_sites <- grouped_cv_folds(surveys$site, k = 3, ids = rownames(surveys))  habitat_new   <- cross_validate_mixed(count ~ habitat + (1 | site), surveys,                                       new_sites, family = "poisson",                                       prediction = "new_group") intercept_new <- cross_validate_mixed(count ~ 1 + (1 | site), surveys,                                       new_sites, family = "poisson",                                       prediction = "new_group") mixed_tab <- cv_tab(list(habitat = habitat_new, intercept = intercept_new),                     metric = "neg_log_score") mixed_tab[, c("Modnames", "Rank", "Score", "Delta", "Unit")] #>    Modnames Rank    Score    Delta                        Unit #> 1   habitat    1 1.986689 0.000000 joint_group_density_per_row #> 2 intercept    2 2.208725 0.222036 joint_group_density_per_row # Later visits: train on visits 1 to 6, predict visits 7 and 8 at every site ids <- rownames(surveys) later_visits <- list(later = list(analysis   = ids[surveys$visit <= 6],                                   assessment = ids[surveys$visit > 6])) habitat_later <- cross_validate_mixed(count ~ habitat + (1 | site), surveys,                                       later_visits, family = "poisson",                                       prediction = "existing_group") habitat_later$summary[, c("metric", "estimate", "n_assessment")] #>          metric estimate n_assessment #> 1 neg_log_score 2.118291           36 #> 2          rmse 2.553329           36

code: library(multiScaleR) library(terra)  # 1. Prepare the data data("landscape_counts"); data("surv_pts") pts  <- vect(surv_pts) land <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif", package = "multiScaleR")) inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land, max_D = 1700,                       kernel = "gaussian", bin = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) dat <- data.frame(landscape_counts, inputs$kernel_dat)  # 2. Build folds that match the prediction question folds <- spatial_cv_folds(crds(pts), block_size = 1000, k = 3, crs = 32617) folds_buffer <- spatial_cv_folds(crds(pts), block_size = 1000, k = 3,                                  buffer = 320, crs = 32617) site_id <- rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"), each = 2)   # group per row grouped <- grouped_cv_folds(site_id, k = 3, ids = paste0("visit", 1:12))  # 3. Cross-validate: scales and coefficients are re-estimated in every fold cv <- cross_validate(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, data = dat,                      kernel_inputs = inputs, folds = folds,                      family = "poisson", keep_selection = TRUE) cv                      # pooled scores, lower is better cv$complete             # TRUE: every fold was fitted and scored cv$training             # scales and coefficients estimated in each fold  # 4. Reference models on the same folds null_cv <- cross_validate_glm(counts ~ 1, dat, folds, family = "poisson",                               keep_selection = TRUE) site_cv <- cross_validate_glm(counts ~ site, dat, folds, family = "poisson",                               keep_selection = TRUE) candidates <- list(landscape = cv, site_only = site_cv, null = null_cv)  # 5. Compare cv_tab(candidates, metric = "rmse")                   # pooled, in counts cv_tab(candidates, metric = "neg_log_score")          # whole distribution cv_tab(candidates, metric = "rmse", by_fold = TRUE)   # is the ranking consistent?  # 6. Score an AICc selection rule selected <- select_cv(candidates, criterion = "AICc") selected$selection$chosen                             # model chosen per fold  # 7. Repeated surveys: choose the prediction target, then compare candidates new_sites <- grouped_cv_folds(surveys$site, k = 3, ids = rownames(surveys)) habitat_new <- cross_validate_mixed(count ~ habitat + (1 | site), surveys,                                     new_sites, family = "poisson",                                     prediction = "new_group")   # unseen sites intercept_new <- cross_validate_mixed(count ~ 1 + (1 | site), surveys,                                       new_sites, family = "poisson",                                       prediction = "new_group") cv_tab(list(habitat = habitat_new, intercept = intercept_new),        metric = "neg_log_score")                    # joint score per survey

code: # Holds the estimated scales fixed cond  <- predict(fit, interval = "confidence", uncertainty = "conditional")  # Lets scales and coefficients vary together joint <- predict(fit, interval = "confidence", uncertainty = "joint")  compare <- data.frame(   expected    = cond$fit,   cond_lower  = cond$lower,  cond_upper  = cond$upper,   joint_lower = joint$lower, joint_upper = joint$upper ) round(head(compare, 5), 2) #>   expected cond_lower cond_upper joint_lower joint_upper #> 1     0.91       0.67       1.23        0.67        1.23 #> 2     2.58       1.83       3.63        1.64        4.07 #> 3     4.69       3.85       5.70        3.59        6.12 #> 4     2.05       1.70       2.46        1.54        2.72 #> 5     2.00       1.42       2.81        1.40        2.84 # Ten survey points spread across the range of expected counts keep <- order(compare$expected)[seq(5, 95, by = 10)] long <- data.frame(   point    = factor(rep(seq_along(keep), 2)),   expected = rep(compare$expected[keep], 2),   lower    = c(compare$cond_lower[keep], compare$joint_lower[keep]),   upper    = c(compare$cond_upper[keep], compare$joint_upper[keep]),   interval = rep(c("Conditional", "Joint"), each = length(keep)) )  ggplot(long, aes(x = point, y = expected, ymin = lower, ymax = upper,                  color = interval)) +   geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +   scale_color_manual(values = c(Conditional = "black", Joint = "#2166AC")) +   labs(x = "Survey point (ordered by expected count)",        y = "Expected count", color = "Interval") +   theme_classic() # How much wider is the joint interval at each of the 100 survey points? ratio <- (joint$upper - joint$lower) / (cond$upper - cond$lower) round(quantile(ratio, c(0, 0.5, 1)), 2) #>   0%  50% 100%  #> 1.00 1.14 2.08

code: set.seed(321)  # A 200 x 200 grid of 20 m cells in a projected CRS, so map units are meters noise <- rast(nrows = 200, ncols = 200, xmin = 0, xmax = 4000,               ymin = 0, ymax = 4000, crs = "EPSG:32617") values(noise) <- rnorm(ncell(noise))  # Smooth the noise and cut it at zero to get patches of forest forest <- focal(noise, w = focalMat(noise, 100, "Gauss"), fun = "sum",                 na.rm = TRUE) > 0 forest <- forest * 1                   # logical to numeric 0/1 names(forest) <- "forest" plot(forest) # The landscape as the animal perceives it: forest weighted by the true kernel true_sigma <- 150 perceived  <- focal(forest, w = focalMat(forest, true_sigma, "Gauss"),                     fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)  n_sets <- 400                          # choice sets (one per observed step) n_alt  <- 5                            # candidate end points per choice set  # Each choice set starts at a random location away from the map edge. # Candidates leave it in a random direction with a random step length (m). start_x <- rep(runif(n_sets, 1000, 3000), each = n_alt) start_y <- rep(runif(n_sets, 1000, 3000), each = n_alt) step_m  <- rgamma(n_sets * n_alt, shape = 2, scale = 100) angle   <- runif(n_sets * n_alt, 0, 2 * pi)  steps <- data.frame(   step_id = rep(seq_len(n_sets), each = n_alt),   # choice-set ID   x       = start_x + step_m * cos(angle),   y       = start_y + step_m * sin(angle),   sl_km   = step_m / 1000                         # step length in km )  # Perceived forest at each end point, standardized across all end points f <- extract(perceived, as.matrix(steps[, c("x", "y")]))[, 1] z <- (f - mean(f)) / sd(f)  # True selection: +1 per standard deviation of forest, -3 per km of step. # The animal takes exactly one candidate per choice set. score <- exp(1 * z - 3 * steps$sl_km) steps$case_ <- 0 for (s in seq_len(n_sets)) {   rows <- which(steps$step_id == s)   steps$case_[sample(rows, 1, prob = score[rows])] <- 1 } head(steps, 5) #>   step_id         x        y      sl_km case_ #> 1       1  796.5978 1407.895 0.40284437     0 #> 2       1 1111.5662 1191.215 0.35312305     0 #> 3       1 1135.6157 1525.462 0.04405726     1 #> 4       1 1461.6048 1562.778 0.28484673     0 #> 5       1 1214.1488 1594.263 0.06691232     0

code: data("surv_pts") pts <- vect(surv_pts)      # 100 survey points xy  <- crds(pts)           # their coordinates, in meters land_rast <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                               package = "multiScaleR"))  # Landscape covariates smoothed at the true scales, then standardized truth  <- kernel_scale.raster(land_rast[[c("land1", "land2")]],                               sigma = c(250, 500), kernel = "gaussian",                               verbose = FALSE) x_true <- scale(as.matrix(extract(truth, pts, ID = FALSE)))  set.seed(1) # The field: correlation between two points is exp(-distance / 800) d_mat <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) field <- drop(t(chol(0.6^2 * exp(-d_mat / 800))) %*% rnorm(nrow(xy))) site  <- rnorm(nrow(xy))   # a covariate measured at the survey point  # Log expected count: intercept, site effect, landscape effects, and the field log_mu <- 1 + 0.3 * site - 0.5 * x_true[, "land1"] +   0.7 * x_true[, "land2"] + field dat <- data.frame(counts = rpois(nrow(xy), exp(log_mu)), site = site)

Prepare the kernel inputs data("surv_pts") pts   <- vect(surv_pts) land1 <- rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                           package = "multiScaleR"))[["land1"]] kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land1,                              max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian")  # 2. Simulate a survey (or build the frame from your own records) land1_250 <- kernel_scale.raster(raster_stack = land1, sigma = 250,                                  kernel = "gaussian") hab_true  <- as.numeric(scale(terra::extract(land1_250, pts, ID = FALSE)[, 1])) sim <- sim_dat_gdr(density = exp(log(400) + 0.5 * hab_true),                    distance_scale = 40, removal = 0.2,                    dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75),                    interval_lengths = c(2, 3, 5), interval_units = "minutes",                    site_covs = kernel_inputs$kernel_dat,                    event_keys = data.frame(survey = paste0("pt", 1:100)),                    seed = 2) umf <- sim$observed  # 3. Check the data validate_unmarked_data(object = umf, event_keys = sim$event_keys,                        event_id = "survey", interval_units = "minutes",                        effort = rep(10, 100))$valid  # 4. Fit a starting model, then estimate the scale of effect mod <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~ land1, removalformula = ~ 1,                               distanceformula = ~ 1, data = umf,                               keyfun = "halfnorm", mixture = "P",                               output = "density", unitsOut = "kmsq", K = 60,                               starts = c(log(400), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.2))) opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod, kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs,                         n_cores = 1)  # 5. Read the results summary(opt)                                  # sigma, effective distance, model fit <- opt$opt_mod unmarked::predict(fit, type = "lambda")       # density, birds per square km unmarked::predict(fit, type = "dist")         # distance scale, m unmarked::predict(fit, type = "rem")          # removal probability per minute plot(opt)                                     # kernel weight against distance plot_marginal_effects(opt, type = "lambda")   # density across the covariate  # 6. Map density r_scaled <- kernel_scale.raster(raster_stack = land1, multiScaleR = opt,                                 scale_center = TRUE, clamp = TRUE) dens_map <- terra::predict(r_scaled, fit, type = "lambda")

title: Rank models by AIC or AICc — aic_tab
code: ## Bundled counts simulated with a habitat scale of 75 map units data("pts") data("count_data") hab <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "hab.tif", package = "multiScaleR")) prepared <- kernel_prep(pts, hab, max_D = 300, sigma = 75, verbose = FALSE) dat <- data.frame(y = count_data$y, prepared$kernel_dat) fixed_model <- glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson(), data = dat) null_model <- glm(y ~ 1, family = poisson(), data = dat) spatial_model <- multiScale_optim(fixed_model, prepared, par = 75 / 300,                                   n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE) models <- list(spatial = spatial_model, fixed = fixed_model, null = null_model)  ## The fixed model already uses the true 75-unit scale, so the spatial model ## reaches the same log-likelihood and pays for one extra parameter (sigma). aic_tab(models, AICc = FALSE, mod_names = names(models)) #>  #> Model selection based on AIC: #>  #>         K    AIC Delta_AIC AICWt Cum.Wt      LL #> fixed   2 232.34      0.00  0.73   0.73 -114.17 #> spatial 3 234.33      1.99  0.27   1.00 -114.17 #> null    1 346.69    114.35  0.00   1.00 -172.34 #>  aic_tab(models, AICc = TRUE, mod_names = names(models)) #>  #> Model selection based on AICc: #>  #>         K   AICc Delta_AICc AICcWt Cum.Wt      LL #> fixed   2 232.51       0.00   0.75   0.75 -114.17 #> spatial 3 234.67       2.16   0.25   1.00 -114.17 #> null    1 346.74     114.23   0.00   1.00 -172.34 #>   ## K for a stored N-mixture fit: three abundance coefficients, one ## detection coefficient, and two estimated scales nmix <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-user-guide-nmix.rds",                             package = "multiScaleR")) aic_tab(list(nmix), mod_names = "bin1 + cont2") #>  #> Model selection based on AICc: #>  #>              K    AICc Delta_AICc AICcWt Cum.Wt      LL #> bin1 + cont2 6 1001.89          0      1      1 -494.33 #>

code: # \donttest{ # The field needs unmarked 1.5.2 and TMB 1.9.25. if (requireNamespace("TMB", quietly = TRUE) &&     utils::packageVersion("unmarked") == "1.5.2" &&     utils::packageVersion("TMB") == "1.9.25") {   # Eight survey blocks 1 km apart along a line, six point counts in each   block <- factor(rep(paste0("b", 1:8), each = 6))   hab <- rep(seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6), 8)   shift <- c(-0.4, -0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.4)[block]   sim <- sim_dat_gdr(density = exp(log(400) + 0.5 * hab + shift),     distance_scale = 40, removal = 0.2, dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75),     interval_lengths = c(2, 3, 5), interval_units = "minutes",     site_covs = data.frame(hab = hab, block = block), seed = 1)   umf <- sim$observed    # Template: an independent random intercept for each block (TMB engine)   template <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~ hab + (1 | block),     removalformula = ~ 1, distanceformula = ~ 1, data = umf,     keyfun = "halfnorm", mixture = "P", output = "density",     unitsOut = "kmsq", K = 60, engine = "TMB",     starts = c(log(400), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.2), log(0.3)))    # Every survey carries the projected coordinates (m) of its block center   block_xy <- cbind(x = 500000 + 1000 * (as.integer(block) - 1),                     y = 4400000)   rownames(block_xy) <- rownames(unmarked::siteCovs(umf))    # A second set of starting values, named by parameter block and position   cold <- c("beta_lambda[1]" = log(300), "beta_lambda[2]" = 0,             "beta_dist[1]" = log(30), "beta_rem[1]" = qlogis(0.4),             "lsigma_lambda[1]" = log(0.5))   settings <- list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L,                    control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10))    field_fit <- fit_gdr_response_field(template, coords = block_xy,     crs = 32617, range = 2000, cold_starts = list(cold = cold),     audit_dir = tempfile("gdr-field-"), tmb_settings = settings)    # Log density, log distance scale (m) and logit removal probability   print(unmarked::coef(field_fit))   # SD of the block deviations, on the log density scale   print(unmarked::sigma(field_fit))   # The range adds no parameter, so the AIC penalty matches the template   print(c(template = template@AIC, field = field_fit@AIC)) } #> lambda(Int) lambda(hab)   dist(Int)    rem(Int)  #>    6.129380    0.442348    3.660080   -1.630779  #>    Model Groups        Name     sigma      lower     upper #> 1 lambda  block (Intercept) 0.2465776 0.09603019 0.6331394 #> template    field  #> 581.9212 580.3834  # }

code: if (as.character(utils::packageVersion("unmarked")) == "1.5.2") {   # Five point counts: birds by distance band and by time interval   yd <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(0, 2), c(2, 1), c(0, 0))   yr <- rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(0, 1, 0), c(1, 0, 1), c(1, 1, 1), c(0, 0, 0))   frame <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR(yd, yr, dist.breaks = c(0, 25, 75),     unitsIn = "m", period.lengths = c(1, 2, 1),     siteCovs = data.frame(hab = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 5)))   # Fit the starting model (C engine) before declaring extra starts   model <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~hab, data = frame,     output = "abund", K = 40, se = FALSE, engine = "C",     starts = c(log(8), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.3)), control = list(maxit = 2000))   # One extra start, named like the model coefficients (link scales)   cold <- unmarked::coef(model)   cold[] <- 0   cold["dist(Int)"] <- log(30)   audit_dir <- tempfile("msr-gdr-audit-")   refit <- make_gdr_refitter(model, list(cold = cold), audit_dir = audit_dir)    # multiScale_optim() calls refit() at each candidate scale. Calling it   # once here, on the original data, shows what each call records.   fit <- refit(model, frame, context = list(covs = "hab"))   audit <- attr(fit, "msr_gdr_refit_audit")   # Log-likelihood and eligibility of each start, then the selected start   print(sapply(audit$attempts, function(a)     c(logLik = a$logLik, eligible = a$eligible)))   print(audit$attempts[[audit$selected]]$name)   # contract.rds, plus request, input, attempt and summary records   print(list.files(audit_dir)) } #>               [,1]      [,2]      [,3] #> logLik   -14.77773 -14.77773 -14.77773 #> eligible   1.00000   1.00000   1.00000 #> [1] "original" #>  [1] "contract.rds"                                            #>  [2] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-1-request.rds" #>  [3] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-1.rds"         #>  [4] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-2-request.rds" #>  [5] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-2.rds"         #>  [6] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-3-request.rds" #>  [7] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-3.rds"         #>  [8] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-input.rds"             #>  [9] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-request.rds"           #> [10] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1.rds"

text: 1D 2D distance: two ways turn sigma distance. 2D distance (default) radius circle around point holds set proportion ideal kernel's weight plane. 1D distance measured along line point shorter. See kernel_dist(). Backend: computational route multiScale_optim() uses search scales, chosen backend argument. See multiScaleR-fitting-methods. Binned inputs: distance-binned summaries kernel_prep() stores bin = TRUE (default). let search compute kernel-weighted means without visiting every cell, much faster. Buffer: set raster cells within max_D survey point. cells contribute point's kernel-weighted covariates. Choice set: step-selection model, one used step together available steps compared . See vignette("v10-step-selection", package = "multiScaleR"). Conditional uncertainty: uncertainty treats estimated scales known. coefficient standard errors prediction intervals conditional. See multiScaleR-prediction. Credible interval: Bayesian interval contains stated posterior probability (example 95 percent) quantity, given model, data, priors. See multiScale_bayes(). Cross-validation: estimating --sample predictive performance fitting model part data (training folds) scoring predictions rest (held-fold). Spatial folds hold blocks nearby points, grouped folds hold whole groups sites years. See cross_validate(). Distance-removal model: model counts recorded distance classes removal intervals separates abundance detection. multiScaleR uses unmarked's generalized distance-removal (GDR) models. See vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR"). Effective distance: distance contains set proportion (default 90 percent) kernel's weight. converts sigma distance map units easy report compare across kernels. See kernel_dist(). Expected response: mean response model predicts given covariate values, expected count occurrence probability. differs observation replicate, simulated new observation also includes observation noise. See multiScaleR-prediction. Exponential power kernel ("expow"): kernel shape parameter addition sigma, lets weight curve range sharply peaked nearly flat-topped. See multiScaleR-kernels. Fixed kernel: kernel gives every cell within radius weight cells beyond weight. scale hard radius. Fixed-radius metric: landscape surface metric computed radius set, scale estimate enters model ordinary covariate. See msr_vars(). Gaussian kernel: default kernel, whose weights decline distance following normal (bell-shaped) curve standard deviation sigma. See multiScaleR-kernels. Hard radius: scale cell either fully fully calculation. Landscape metrics, unweighted surface metrics, fixed kernel use hard radii. likelihood changes steps, get Hessian standard error. Hessian: matrix second derivatives log-likelihood maximum. inverse approximates variance estimates gives Wald standard errors. Joint uncertainty: uncertainty lets scales coefficients vary together, intervals also reflect uncertainty scales. backends provide . See multiScaleR-fitting-methods. Kernel: function assigns weight raster cell according distance survey point. Kernel-weighted covariates summarize landscape around point. See multiScaleR-kernels. Kernel-weighted mean: weighted average raster's cell values around point, using kernel weights. default covariate type, set kernel_var(). Landscape metric: summary composition arrangement land-cover classes within radius, proportion class edge density, set landscape_var(). Laplace approximation: fast approximation treats distribution (posterior, integral random effects) Gaussian around peak. See vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR"). Lean mode: preparing inputs store_cell_data = FALSE, keeps binned summaries save memory. works every covariate kernel-weighted mean. Link scale response scale: generalized linear model works link scale (example log counts log odds) reports predictions response scale (counts probabilities) back-transforming inverse link. See multiScaleR-prediction. Marginal likelihood: likelihood integrating random quantities, random effects -group standard deviation scale. max_D min_D: largest smallest scales search may consider, map units. Set max_D kernel_prep() largest plausible scale effect; min_D set raster resolution. Negative exponential kernel ("exp"): kernel whose weights decline exponentially distance, giving weight nearby cells longer tail Gaussian kernel. See multiScaleR-kernels. Posterior: Bayesian model, probability distribution parameters given data priors. See multiScale_bayes(). Profile likelihood: log-likelihood function one parameter, every parameter re-estimated value. Profile-likelihood intervals follow shape likelihood instead assuming symmetric. See profile_sigma(). Scale effect: distance landscape variable influences response. multiScaleR estimates sigma kernel, kernel_dist() converts effective distance. Shape: second parameter exponential power kernel, controls sharply weights fall . Sigma: scale parameter kernel, map units. larger sigma spreads weight wider area. Sigma distance report; see Effective distance. Spatial response field: spatially correlated random effect captures residual spatial pattern covariates leave unexplained. See vignette("v11-spatial-fields", package = "multiScaleR"). SQ: kernel-weighted root-mean-square deviation continuous surface around local mean, measure surface roughness. See surface_var(). Standardization: centering covariate mean dividing standard deviation. multiScaleR standardizes optimized covariate every candidate scale default, coefficient describes effect one standard deviation change. Step-selection model: model animal movement compares used step available steps conditional logistic regression. See vignette("v10-step-selection", package = "multiScaleR"). Surface metric: summary texture continuous surface around point, roughness skewness, set surface_var(). Wald interval: interval built estimate plus minus multiple standard error. assumes symmetric, nearly quadratic likelihood near estimate, may hold scales.

code: # Estimate the scale of effect of habitat on simulated counts data(pts) data(count_data) hab <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "hab.tif",                                package = "multiScaleR")) inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = hab, max_D = 250,                       kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE) start_model <- glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = count_data) fit <- multiScale_optim(start_model, inputs, verbose = FALSE) summary(fit)   # sigma near the simulated value of 75 map units #>  #> Call: #> multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = start_model, kernel_inputs = inputs,  #>     verbose = FALSE) #>  #>  #> Kernel used: #> gaussian #>  #> ***** Optimized Scale of Effect ***** #>  #>         Mean       SE     2.5%    97.5% #> hab 76.16637 9.567451 57.09847 95.23428 #>  #>  #>   ====================================  #>  #> ***** Optimized Scale of Effect -- Distance ***** #> Scale distances (map units) at 90%, two definitions. #>  #> 2D, radius of the circle for the ideal untruncated kernel (selected): #>       Mean   2.5%  97.5% #> hab 163.45 122.53 204.37 #>  #> 1D, along a line through the point (comparison): #>       Mean  2.5%  97.5% #> hab 125.28 93.92 156.65 #>  #>  #>   ====================================  #>  #>  *****     Fitted Model Summary     ***** #>  #>  #> Call: #> glm(formula = y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = data) #>  #> Coefficients: #>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> (Intercept)   0.4807     0.1021   4.707 2.51e-06 *** #> hab           0.8691     0.0855  10.166  < 2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> (Dispersion parameter for poisson family taken to be 1) #>  #>     Null deviance: 186.585  on 74  degrees of freedom #> Residual deviance:  70.185  on 73  degrees of freedom #> AIC: 232.29 #>  #> Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 5 #>  #>  #>  WARNING!!! #>  The estimated scale of effect approaches or exceeds the current search extent.  #>  Consider increasing max_D in `kernel_prep` to >= 250.56 to ensure accurate estimation of scale. #>  #>  #>  #> ***** Follow-up recommendation ***** #> Recommended `max_D`: 250.56 #> Recommended starting `sigma` values: #>      hab  #> 76.16637  #>  #> Action: #> Refit from the optimized parameters and address the flagged diagnostics.

The bands ## are 95% limits that hold the scales of effect at their estimates. curves <- plot_marginal_effects(fit, ylab = "Expected count")    names(curves) #> [1] "site"  "land1" "land2"  ## The values behind one panel. land1 is back on its original scale, the ## kernel-weighted proportion of habitat around a point. head(curves$land1$data) #>           x      fit      lwr      upr variable #> 1 0.2969672 3.294993 2.574430 4.217237    land1 #> 2 0.3005787 3.218289 2.528560 4.096158    land1 #> 3 0.3041903 3.143370 2.483240 3.978985    land1 #> 4 0.3078019 3.070195 2.438449 3.865611    land1 #> 5 0.3114135 2.998723 2.394169 3.755934    land1 #> 6 0.3150251 2.928916 2.350381 3.649854    land1  # \donttest{ ## A caption stating what the limits include, useful while exploring plot_marginal_effects(fit, ylab = "Expected count", add_label = TRUE)    # }  ## Expected abundance from a stored N-mixture fit, with native 95% ## confidence limits nmix <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-user-guide-nmix.rds",                             package = "multiScaleR")) plot_marginal_effects(nmix, type = "state", ylab = "Expected abundance")

title: Predict from a Distance-Removal Model with a Fixed-Range Abundance Field — predict,unmarkedFitGDRField-method
code: # \donttest{ # The field needs unmarked 1.5.2 and TMB 1.9.25. if (requireNamespace("TMB", quietly = TRUE) &&     utils::packageVersion("unmarked") == "1.5.2" &&     utils::packageVersion("TMB") == "1.9.25") {   # Eight survey blocks 1 km apart, six point counts in each   block <- factor(rep(paste0("b", 1:8), each = 6))   hab <- rep(seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6), 8)   shift <- c(-0.4, -0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.4)[block]   sim <- sim_dat_gdr(density = exp(log(400) + 0.5 * hab + shift),     distance_scale = 40, removal = 0.2, dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75),     interval_lengths = c(2, 3, 5), interval_units = "minutes",     site_covs = data.frame(hab = hab, block = block), seed = 1)   template <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~ hab + (1 | block),     removalformula = ~ 1, distanceformula = ~ 1, data = sim$observed,     keyfun = "halfnorm", mixture = "P", output = "density",     unitsOut = "kmsq", K = 60, engine = "TMB",     starts = c(log(400), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.2), log(0.3)))   block_xy <- cbind(x = 500000 + 1000 * (as.integer(block) - 1),                     y = 4400000)   rownames(block_xy) <- rownames(unmarked::siteCovs(sim$observed))   cold <- c("beta_lambda[1]" = log(300), "beta_lambda[2]" = 0,             "beta_dist[1]" = log(30), "beta_rem[1]" = qlogis(0.4),             "lsigma_lambda[1]" = log(0.5))   settings <- list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L,                    control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10))   field_fit <- fit_gdr_response_field(template, block_xy, crs = 32617,     range = 2000, cold_starts = list(cold = cold),     audit_dir = tempfile("gdr-field-"), tmb_settings = settings)    # Density (birds per square km) at average habitat: in block b3, at a   # point halfway between blocks b3 and b4, and with the field set to zero   in_block <- predict(field_fit, type = "lambda",     newdata = data.frame(hab = 0, block = factor("b3", levels(block))))   between <- predict(field_fit, type = "lambda",     newdata = data.frame(hab = 0), coords = cbind(502500, 4400000),     crs = 32617)   no_field <- predict(field_fit, type = "lambda",     newdata = data.frame(hab = 0), re.form = NA)   dens <- rbind(in_block, between, no_field)   rownames(dens) <- c("block b3", "between b3 and b4", "no field")   print(dens)   # The SE between blocks adds field variance left after conditioning on   # the fitted blocks (both variances on the log scale)   u <- attr(between, "response_field_uncertainty")   print(c(fitted = unname(u$fitted_joint_predictor_variance),           between_blocks = unname(u$new_field_residual_predictor_variance)))   # Removal probability per minute, one row per survey and interval   print(head(predict(field_fit, type = "rem"), 3)) } #>                   Predicted        SE    lower    upper #> block b3           378.4863  85.53074 243.0495 589.3939 #> between b3 and b4  423.9838  94.82578 273.5107 657.2402 #> no field           459.1513 100.73197 298.6847 705.8276 #>         fitted between_blocks  #>     0.03513006     0.01489118  #>   Predicted         SE     lower     upper #> 1 0.1637236 0.02684601 0.1176291 0.2233096 #> 2 0.1637236 0.02684601 0.1176291 0.2233096 #> 3 0.1637236 0.02684601 0.1176291 0.2233096 # code: ## Running example: counts at 100 survey points and two landscape layers data("landscape_counts") data("surv_pts") pts <- terra::vect(surv_pts) land <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                                 package = "multiScaleR"))[[c("land1", "land2")]]  ## The simulated layers are in meters but carry no coordinate reference ## system. Declare a local planar one so raster prediction can check cells. terra::crs(land) <- "local" terra::crs(pts) <- "local"  ## bin = TRUE stores the distance bins that the analytic backend needs inputs <- kernel_prep(pts, land, max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian",                       bin = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) dat <- data.frame(landscape_counts, inputs$kernel_dat) start <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, family = poisson(), data = dat) fit <- multiScale_optim(start, inputs, backend = "profile_glm",                         n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)  ## Expected counts at the first three survey points predict(fit)[1:3] #>         1         2         3  #> 0.9066805 2.5784219 4.6877074   ## 95% limits for the expected count. Joint limits let the scales vary, ## conditional limits hold them at their estimates. joint <- predict(fit, interval = "confidence") cond <- predict(fit, interval = "confidence", uncertainty = "conditional") round(cbind(expected = joint$fit,             joint_lower = joint$lower, joint_upper = joint$upper,             cond_lower = cond$lower, cond_upper = cond$upper)[1:3, ], 2) #>   expected joint_lower joint_upper cond_lower cond_upper #> 1     0.91        0.67        1.23       0.67       1.23 #> 2     2.58        1.64        4.07       1.83       3.63 #> 3     4.69        3.59        6.12       3.85       5.70  ## Back-transform a link-scale prediction yourself: exponentiate the ## estimate and its limits, never the standard error. This reproduces the ## joint limits for the first point. eta <- predict(fit, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE) exp(eta$fit[1] + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * eta$se.fit[1]) #> [1] 0.669071 1.228673  ## New points: prepare their landscape with the fitted settings, then give ## site values whose row names ("1", "2", "3") match the prepared point IDs new_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts[1:3], land, max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian",                           bin = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) new_sites <- data.frame(site = c(-1, 0, 1)) predict(fit, new_sites, new_inputs, se.fit = TRUE) #> $fit #>         1         2         3  #> 0.6399094 1.8208897 5.2991735  #>  #> $se.fit #>         1         2         3  #> 0.1278956 0.3456957 0.8556013  #>  #> $type #> [1] "response" #>  #> $uncertainty #> [1] "joint" #>   ## Map the expected count and its conditional standard error. The site ## layer holds the mean of site, so the map describes an average site. layers <- kernel_scale.raster(land, multiScaleR = fit, scale_center = TRUE,                               match_buffer = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) count_map <- predict(fit, layers, se.fit = TRUE, uncertainty = "conditional") terra::plot(count_map)

Abundance ## depends on the bin1 and cont2 layers of a simulated landscape. nmix <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-user-guide-nmix.rds",                             package = "multiScaleR")) layers <- subset(sim_rast(user_seed = 999, dim = 250), c("bin1", "cont2"))  ## Three new sites, prepared with the fitted kernel, max_D, covariate ## definitions, and binning new_pts <- terra::vect(cbind(x = c(800, 1250, 1700),                              y = c(900, 1250, 1600))) new_inputs <- kernel_prep(new_pts, layers, max_D = nmix$max_D,                           kernel = nmix$kernel_inputs$kernel,                           scale_vars = nmix$kernel_inputs$scale_vars,                           bin = !is.null(nmix$kernel_inputs$binned),                           verbose = FALSE)  ## Keys follow the prepared point order. Site B appears twice, for ## example in two survey years, and reuses the same spatial values. keys <- data.frame(site = c("A", "B", "C")) scenarios <- data.frame(site = c("A", "B", "B", "C")) nd <- prepare_unmarked_data(nmix, scenarios, new_inputs, join_by = keys) nd  # bin1 and cont2 in training standard-deviation units #>   site       bin1     cont2 #> 1    A  0.8463096 0.9121894 #> 2    B  1.6378884 0.6597968 #> 3    B  1.6378884 0.6597968 #> 4    C -1.1986195 0.6290868  ## Expected abundance at each row, with native 95% confidence limits unmarked::predict(nmix$opt_mod, type = "state", newdata = nd) #>   Predicted        SE     lower     upper #> 1 2.2541203 0.3245970 1.6998190 2.9891759 #> 2 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771 #> 3 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771 #> 4 0.7324141 0.1144437 0.5392024 0.9948591  ## The same rows and component as a reusable snapshot prepared <- prepare_prediction(nmix, scenarios, new_inputs,                                component = "state", join_by = keys) predict(prepared) #>   Predicted        SE     lower     upper #> 1 2.2541203 0.3245970 1.6998190 2.9891759 #> 2 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771 #> 3 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771 #> 4 0.7324141 0.1144437 0.5392024 0.9948591

50 survey points   xy <- terra::crds(pts)    # Counts depend on habitat at a 400 m scale plus a correlated field   set.seed(3)   truth <- kernel_scale.raster(land, sigma = 400, kernel = "gaussian",                                verbose = FALSE)   x2 <- as.numeric(scale(terra::extract(truth, pts, ID = FALSE)[, 1]))   field <- drop(t(chol(0.25 * exp(-as.matrix(stats::dist(xy)) / 800))) %*%                   stats::rnorm(nrow(xy)))   inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land, max_D = 1200,                         kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)   df <- data.frame(counts = stats::rpois(nrow(xy), exp(1 + 0.6 * x2 + field)),                    inputs$kernel_dat)   df$pos <- glmmTMB::numFactor(xy[, 1], xy[, 2])   # field positions (m)   df$grp <- factor("all")                          # one shared field   m0 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(counts ~ land2 + exp(pos + 0 | grp),                          family = poisson(), data = df,                          start = list(theta = c(log(0.5), log(500))))   fit <- multiScale_optim(m0, inputs, n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)    # title: Profile and Bootstrap Inference for an NB2 Scale — scale_inference
code: # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(42)   habitat <- terra::rast(nrows = 60, ncols = 60, xmin = 0, xmax = 600,                          ymin = 0, ymax = 600, crs = "EPSG:32617")   cells <- seq_len(terra::ncell(habitat))   terra::values(habitat) <- sin(cells / 41) + cos(cells / 73)   names(habitat) <- "hab"   sites <- terra::vect(expand.grid(x = seq(150, 450, length.out = 6),                                   y = seq(150, 450, length.out = 6)),                        geom = c("x", "y"), crs = terra::crs(habitat))   ki <- kernel_prep(sites, habitat, max_D = 120, bin = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)   dat <- data.frame(ki$kernel_dat)   dat$y <- rnbinom(nrow(dat), mu = exp(.5 + dat$hab), size = 2)   initial <- glm(y ~ hab, data = dat, family = MASS::negative.binomial(2))   fit <- multiScale_optim(initial, ki, backend = "profile_glm",                            n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)   assessment <- scale_inference(fit, grid_points = 9, n_starts = 2)   assessment$profile_set   # Separate regions, with explicit search bounds.   assessment$diagnostics  # A broad region may leave scale unresolved. } #> Warning: Joint Wald uncertainty unavailable: Poisson limit within the diagnostic likelihood threshold. code: ## Running example: counts at 100 survey points, two landscape layers data("landscape_counts") data("surv_pts") pts <- terra::vect(surv_pts) land <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",                                 package = "multiScaleR"))[[c("land1", "land2")]] inputs <- kernel_prep(pts, land, max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian",                       bin = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) dat <- data.frame(landscape_counts, inputs$kernel_dat) start <- glm(counts ~ site + land1 + land2, family = poisson(), data = dat) fit <- multiScale_optim(start, inputs, backend = "profile_glm",                         n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)  ## Joint covariance of the two log scales and four coefficients V <- vcov(fit) round(V, 4) #>                  log_scale:land1 log_scale:land2 beta:(Intercept) beta:site #> log_scale:land1           0.0193          0.0011          -0.0002    0.0002 #> log_scale:land2           0.0011          0.0090          -0.0005   -0.0014 #> beta:(Intercept)         -0.0002         -0.0005           0.0083   -0.0016 #> beta:site                 0.0002         -0.0014          -0.0016    0.0070 #> beta:land1               -0.0009         -0.0020           0.0030   -0.0015 #> beta:land2                0.0014          0.0020          -0.0034    0.0001 #>                  beta:land1 beta:land2 #> log_scale:land1     -0.0009     0.0014 #> log_scale:land2     -0.0020     0.0020 #> beta:(Intercept)     0.0030    -0.0034 #> beta:site           -0.0015     0.0001 #> beta:land1           0.0068    -0.0008 #> beta:land2          -0.0008     0.0058  ## 95% Wald limits for sigma, in meters, from the log-scale standard errors. ## They match the limits in summary(fit). se_log <- sqrt(diag(V))[c("log_scale:land1", "log_scale:land2")] sigma <- stats::setNames(fit$scale_est$Mean, rownames(fit$scale_est)) round(cbind(sigma, lower = sigma * exp(-qnorm(0.975) * se_log),             upper = sigma * exp(qnorm(0.975) * se_log))) #>       sigma lower upper #> land1   238   182   313 #> land2   500   415   602  ## Correlations show how the scale and coefficient estimates trade off round(cov2cor(V), 2) #>                  log_scale:land1 log_scale:land2 beta:(Intercept) beta:site #> log_scale:land1             1.00            0.08            -0.02      0.02 #> log_scale:land2             0.08            1.00            -0.06     -0.17 #> beta:(Intercept)           -0.02           -0.06             1.00     -0.20 #> beta:site                   0.02           -0.17            -0.20      1.00 #> beta:land1                 -0.08           -0.26             0.40     -0.21 #> beta:land2                  0.13            0.28            -0.49      0.02 #>                  beta:land1 beta:land2 #> log_scale:land1       -0.08       0.13 #> log_scale:land2       -0.26       0.28 #> beta:(Intercept)       0.40      -0.49 #> beta:site             -0.21       0.02 #> beta:land1             1.00      -0.12 #> beta:land2            -0.12       1.00  ## Coefficient standard errors with and without scale uncertainty round(cbind(joint = sqrt(diag(V))[-(1:2)],             conditional = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit, type = "conditional")))), 3) #>                  joint conditional #> beta:(Intercept) 0.091       0.091 #> beta:site        0.084       0.082 #> beta:land1       0.082       0.079 #> beta:land2       0.076       0.072
